3. It was alleged that the plaintiff was the rightful owner and possessor of above 58 decimal land and he transferred above land for a consideration of Taka 4,500 to the defendant by registered kobla deed dated 5-7-1987. In the same sitting and by the same scribe a deed of ekrarnama was written and executed by defendant No.1 stipulating the return of the disputed land to the plaintiff if within two years above consideration money was refunded. The plaintiff offered the return of above consideration money and return of possession of above land to the defendant but he refused. The plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.XII/12/87-88 to the Assistant Commissioner (land) under section 95ka of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. But the Assistant Commissioner rejected above case on the ground of non-registration of the ekrarnama. Against above order the plaintiff preferred an appeal to the Additional Deputy commissioner, Dinajpur which was dismissed. 

 4. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing-a written statement alleging that above deed of Ekrarnama dated 15-6-1987 was not executed by the defendant and the same was a forged document. 

 9. Mr ARM Hasanuzzaman, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits, that an ekrarnama as mentioned in section 95(ka) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act cannot be specifically enforced. A special procedure has been laid down in section 95 of the above Act for recovery of possession of a land of a usufractory mortgage. The plaintiff filed a case before the Assistant Commissioner land for redemption of the disputed property but the same was correctly dismissed and an appeal to the ADC (Rev.) against above judgment and order was also dismissed. This suit is misconceived one and the learned Judges of the courts below have failed to appreciate the same. The impugned judgment and decree is vitiated by illegality and the same is note tenable in law. 

 10. On the other hand, Mr Md Hamidur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the opposite party refers to the case of Abdul Kader and another vs Abdul Aziz having died-his heirs; (1) Musammat Masuda Begum and others reported in 47 DM? at page 67 and submits that an agreement for reconveyance can be specifically enforced. The plaintiff proceeded under the provision of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and filed a petition before the Assistant Commissioner land for recovery of possession of the disputed land. But unfortunately that was rejected and an appeal against above unlawful order was also dismissed. Plaintiff has succeeded to prove by consistent and mutually supportive evidence of 5 competent witnesses that the impugned deed of Ekrarnama (Exhibit 1) was a genuine document executed by defendant No. 1 in the same sitting of execution of the impugned kobla deed. On consideration of above materials on record the learned Judges of both the courts below have rightly and concurrently held that the plaintiff was entitled to get back possession of the disputed land and accordingly decreed the suit and dismissed the appeal respectively which calls for no interference. 

 13. As PW 1 plaintiff gave evidence in this suit and reiterated his claims as set out in the plaint that in the same sitting the defendant executed a deed of Ekrarnama providing for reconveyance of the disputed land within 2 (two) years if the plaintiff returns the consideration money. The witness produced above Ekrarnama deed which was marked as Exhibit 1. PW 2 Jatindra Nath stated that he was the scribe of both the registered kobla deed dated 15-6-1987 (Exhibit 1 . (ka) and the disputed deed of Ekrarnama (Exhibit No.1) Above two deeds were written and executed in the same sitting and the defendant executed above deed of Ekrarnama. PW 3 Abul Kashem was the attesting witness of above two documents, the registered kobla deed dated 15-6-1987 and the impugned deed of Ekrarnama. This witness has stated that he identified defendant No.1 in both the documents. 

 15. It is proved by above legal evidence that defendant No.1 executed above Ekramama in the same sitting when registered kobla deed dated 15- 6-1987 was executed and above two documents together makes above transfer of the disputed land by the plaintiff to the defendant an usufractory mortgaged for 7 years as defined in section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 16. It is well settled that any agreement which was executed by the parties voluntarily and knowingly and which dose not contain any illegal terms can be enforced judicially. Since the deed of Ekramama Exhibit 1 is a legal document written and executed under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the same is legally enforceable by a competent Court of law.
